writer.name: Claude Opus 5.5, the hypnosis guide lane's writer (the splices and their fixes; the words are Emulate's)

findings.label: B7 short landing at paragraph end
examples: What will you do at the end?
findings.reason: The linter sees the draft alone. In the article it isn't the paragraph's end: the recording line and the stop lines follow (CONTEXT.txt).

findings.label: D9 follows the source order
examples: 1/1 paragraphs follow the source's points in its order (agreement 1.00); fine if each part notices something; check T13 and T09 in the tell ledger
findings.reason: It is Emulate's rewrite of the words it replaces (SOURCE.txt), so it follows their points in order by design; the turns are Emulate's own ("Decide to do it", "etc." for "Something else?", the questions split).

findings.label: E23 paragraph of instructions
examples: Decide to do it. How will you coax yourself to do this? Make it spacious? Make it warm and...
findings.reason: The paragraph prepares the session in steps, as the paragraph it replaces did and as his published one does ("Decide what kind of encouragement is welcome ... Preview eye closure, any repeated exit and re-entry, and the return."); the change rewords the steps, it adds none.

findings.label: E36/E41 heavy second person
findings.reason: The guide speaks to the reader as "you" throughout; here the "you"s are the reader preparing his own session, as in the paragraph it replaces.

findings.label: O29 a run of three or more questions (gate step 7: "a few shared AI micro-patterns (question runs, triads, "isn't X, it's Y")"; its prediction review: "questions the text answers itself"): keep the ones a reader would ask
examples: 3 questions: Will you close your eyes? Will you come out and go back in again? What will you do at the end?
findings.reason: The three preview questions are his published preview ("Preview eye closure, any repeated exit and re-entry, and the return") as questions the reader asks himself, as in the paragraph it replaces; the text doesn't answer them, the reader does.

findings.label: R1 action "it" near a paragraph start: name the thing (Joel 2026-09-30, on "If you did it": "the first it is unclear referent")
findings.reason: "it" is the induction, the subject of the section ("Before you begin") and of the paragraphs before; the paragraph it replaces opened the same way ("Deciding to do it.").
